messages:
eve.customer: Hey team — started seeing a big p95/p99 regression on non-streaming responses since last night. Streaming TTFB looks fine (first chunk arrives quickly) but non-streaming total time is 2-3x what it used to be. Affects /v1/generate POSTs with ~2k token prompts. Customer traffic spikes show user-facing timeouts.

amy.support: Sorry you're hitting this, @eve. Can you share a sample request id and whether you used streaming=false intentionally? Also which region and model?

eve.customer: request id r-8a2f3c, region us-west1, model redwood-v1-large. We always call streaming=false for this endpoint. No recent change on our side.

amy.support: Thanks — looping in oncall. @maya-oncall can you pick this up?

maya-oncall: Looking. Quick sanity checks: are you seeing any increased 5xxs or just latency? Also are you going through a customer proxy or CDN (e.g., Cloudflare)?

eve.customer: No 5xxs, just high p95/p99. We do go via our internal edge + GCP LB. We tested direct to Redwood API endpoint from a laptop and still saw the slower total time (not as bad but noticeable).

amy.support: Reproducing logs would help. Can you run a curl test toggling streaming on/off and paste outputs? Example I ask customers to run: 

```
# non-streaming
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","prompt":"<~2k tokens>","stream":false}' -w '\nHTTP_TIME:%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null

# streaming
curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","prompt":"<~2k tokens>","stream":true}' -w '\nHTTP_TIME:%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null
```

maya-oncall: Also try the streaming request with `--no-buffer` (`-N`) to avoid local buffering. If streaming TTFB is good but non-streaming is slow it often points at server-side chunk coalescing changes or downstream buffering at reverse proxies.

charlie-runtime: I pulled r-8a2f3c traces from the runtime. For that request id we see normal generation time (~1.1s) but post-generation transfer time increased from ~200ms to ~900ms for non-streaming responses in the last deploy window. Streaming responses still flushed first chunk at ~120ms.

dana-prodeng: Noted — we shipped a change last night to the output coalescer: we moved from sending smaller flushes to a buffer-first coalesce to reduce token overhead (rollout to ~80% of hosts). That mitigates cost but can increase tail for non-streaming aggregated responses when kernel Nagle / proxy buffering interacts badly.

amy.support: That matches the symptoms: streaming keeps flushing early, non-streaming waits for end-of-response or a larger coalesce window leading to higher total time and p95/p99.

maya-oncall: Short term mitigation options we can push: 1) quick rollback of coalescer heuristic for dedicated serving path, or 2) add a special-case: if request header `x-client-prefer-low-latency: 1` present, force smaller flush windows (preserve current behavior for customers that prefer cost).

charlie-runtime: I can prepare a hotfix to add the header override and a conservative default for customers who opt in. Also will add a metric to detect large transfer delay delta between generation end and response complete.

eve.customer: We can add that header, thanks. How fast can that land?

dana-prodeng: If we push header-gated fast-flush it’s a cfg toggle + config rollout — I can get a canary in ~2 hours and full rollout in ~6 hours after smoke tests. For immediate relief we can also toggle the coalescer rollback on the affected pool, but that costs extra token ops.

amy.support: For your team: try adding header `x-client-prefer-low-latency: 1` in your requests and re-run the curl tests. If that removes the regression we’ll proceed with the canary rollout.

eve.customer: Added header and re-ran the curl test — non-streaming time dropped back to expected range. p95 looks good locally. Thank you.

maya-oncall: Good repro. I'll keep monitoring traces for r-8a2f3c family and watch p95/p99 across the pool. @charlie-runtime please proceed with the header override canary.

charlie-runtime: Will do. I'll post the canary job id when live. Also adding follow-ups: (1) audit proxy/coalescer interactions (Nagle, TCP_CORK) (2) improve docs recommending the header for latency-sensitive non-streaming workflows (3) consider a server-side heuristic that detects client connection semantics and adjusts flush windows automatically.

amy.support: Closing loop with @eve: we'll update you once canary is verified and a wider rollout plan is decided. If anything regresses DM me and we'll escalate to rollback. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident annotated: INC-2026-4490012345 — initial reports of non-streaming tail latency regression, mitigation in progress.

amy.support: Thread summary: cause = coalescer rollout interacting with downstream buffering; short-term = header opt-in `x-client-prefer-low-latency: 1`; medium-term = canary rollout of header override and metrics + docs.

eve.customer: Appreciated, please share expected ETA for full rollout so we can plan.

dana-prodeng: ETA full rollout ~6 hours after canary if no regressions. Will post updates here.

amy.support: Thanks everyone — followups will appear in this thread.
